entities.text: Imjamul Haque Biswas  @ Injamul Haque Biswas
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in this case.

Learned Counsel has also pointed out that although the learned Trial Judge has acquitted the appellant from the charge under Section 376(2)(f)(n) of the Indian Penal Code, but he has been convicted under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, which is a similar offence as under Section 376(2)(f)(n) IPC.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: This goes to show that the learned Trial Judge did not apply his mind.

2. Learned Counsel has also pointed out that no certificate under Section 65B of the IT Act was proved before the learned Trial Court and the petitioner has also been acquitted from the charges under Sections 66/67 of the IT Act.
The petitioner is in custody for about three years and there is no chance of an early hearing of the appeal.
3. Learned Counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail.
According to her, there is sufficient incriminating evidence against the present petitioner.

She has also drawn our attention to the Imjamul Haque Biswas vs Unknown on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180851100/
1 deposition of two minor victim girls and according to her their depositions are sufficient to inspire confidence for the offence committed against them by the appellant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As the paper books are ready,
there is no reason for enlarging them on bail.
It is also pointed out that the petitioner's prayer for suspension of sentence was rejected by a Coordinate Bench on January 3, 2025.
4. We have considered the materials on record.

It appears that although the prosecution has contended that the victims were blackmailed by showing some pictures, but the learned Trial Judge acquitted the petitioner from the charges under Sections 66/67 of the IT Act.
There is an inordinate and unexplained delay in lodging the first information report.
The medical evidence appears to be inconclusive.
It is also found that by an order dated January 3, 2025, paper books were directed to be prepared within eight weeks, but although the paper books were ready, the appeal was not heard.
There is no chance of an early hearing of the appeal since the other appeals filed much prior in point of time are yet to be heard.
5. In view of the aforesaid, we allow this application and suspend the sentence of imprisonment imposed upon the applicant/appellant till disposal of the appeal.

6. Accordingly, we direct that the applicant/appellant, namely Imjamul Haque Biswas @ Injamul Haque Biswas shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/-, with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Krishnagar, Nadia, and on further conditions that he shall remain within the jurisdiction of Chapra Police Station until further order and shall meet the Inspector in charge/Officer in charge, Chapra Police Station once in a fortnight till disposal of the appeal.

entities.text: Imjamul Haque Biswas @ Injamul Haque Biswas
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: The petitioner shall not enter the territorial jurisdiction of the concerned police station (Palashipara Police Station) where the victim girls reside.

The applicant shall be personally present or shall be represented by his Counsel during hearing of the appeal and he shall surrender before the Trial Court as and when called for in connection with the present appeal.

7. The department is directed to forward a copy of this order to the Superintendent of the concerned Correctional Home for immediate release of the applicant/appellant unless he is wanted in connection with any other case.

8. We clarify that the observations made by us in this order are only for the purpose of disposing of the application for suspension of sentence and the same shall have no relevance at the final hearing of the appeal.
9. The application being CRAN 2 of 2025 is accordingly disposed of.
10. All parties shall act in terms of server copy of the order downloaded from the official website of this Court.

(Arijit Banerjee, J.) (Apurba Sinha Ray, J.)
